items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: I got the gig with Gerry Mulligan immediately and got a chance to play with Al Cohn and Bob Brookmeyer and the Vanguard band and the list goes on.

ctx.x: I’m crazy. I’m fearless. You know I moved to Los Angeles with 50 dollars in the bank. Seriously. And I had – I don’t think I had one contact. I knew Terry Trotter, the marvelous pianist, through his records, and I called Terry before I got to Los Angeles and told him I was going to be moving up and I’d love to meet him. And we became friends. We used to play four-hand classical music at his Steinway. And Terry recommended me for some gigs almost immediately. And then I fell in with other musicians like Mike Lang…

opportunity to play with people in New York which I did. I got the gig with Gerry Mulligan immediately and got a chance to play with Al Cohn and Bob Brookmeyer and the Vanguard band and the list goes on.

Before we leave Los Angeles so to speak, I wanted to read two quotes from gentlemen who were incredibly successful in that scene but they had different feelings about it. And they’ll remain anonymous but I know that you would know of them. The first fellow said, “L.A. is an incredible place for craft. You really learn to play your instrument, to play in tune, to show up on time, all of the essentials for a craft are there but your soul, your spirit, is not usually nurtured.” The second fellow said, “Our job was…
